    <title>Rust 1.98.0</title>
    <content type="html"><p><a id="user-content-1.98.0-Language"></a></p>
<h2>Language</h2>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/149219" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/149219/hovercard">Allow shortening lifetime of <code>&amp;mut</code> when unsize-coercing, even in an invariant position.</a> For example, you can now coerce a <code>Cell&lt;&amp;'long mut i32&gt;</code> to a <code>Cell&lt;&amp;'short mut dyn Send&gt;</code>. Such shortenings were already previously allowed when coercing a <code>&amp;mut</code> to a <code>&amp;</code>, or coercing a <code>&amp;</code> to a <code>&amp;</code>.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/155521" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/155521/hovercard">Add deny-by-default <code>invalid_runtime_symbol_definitions</code> lint and warn-by-default <code>suspicious_runtime_symbol_definitions</code> lint</a>
<ul>
<li>The lints currently specifically targets <code>core</code> runtime symbols like <code>memcmp</code>, <code>memset</code>, <code>strlen</code>, ... and is planned to be expanded in the next few releases.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/156379" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/156379/hovercard">Add warn-by-default <code>c_void_returns</code> lint to check <code>core::ffi::c_void</code> as a return type</a></li>
</ul>
<p><a id="user-content-1.98.0-Platform-Support"></a></p>
<h2>Platform Support</h2>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/144220" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/144220/hovercard">Add <code>powerpc64-unknown-linux-gnuelfv2</code> as Tier 3</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/155722" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/155722/hovercard">Add <code>aarch64-unknown-linux-pauthtest</code> as Tier 3 target</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/155763" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/155763/hovercard">Promote <code>thumbv7a-none-eabi</code> to Tier 2</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/155763" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/155763/hovercard">Promote <code>thumbv7a-none-eabihf</code> to Tier 2</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/155763" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/155763/hovercard">Promote <code>thumbv7r-none-eabi</code> to Tier 2</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/155763" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/155763/hovercard">Promote <code>thumbv7r-none-eabihf</code> to Tier 2</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/155763" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/155763/hovercard">Promote <code>thumbv8r-none-eabihf</code> to Tier 2</a></li>
</ul>
<p>Refer to Rust's <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustc/platform-support.html" rel="nofollow">platform support page</a> for more information on Rust's tiered platform support.</p>
<p><a id="user-content-1.98.0-Libraries"></a></p>
<h2>Libraries</h2>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/146561" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/146561/hovercard">Change <code>Location&lt;'_&gt;</code> lifetime to <code>'static</code> in <code>Panic[Hook]Info</code></a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/155421" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/155421/hovercard">Document panic in <code>RangeInclusive::from(legacy::RangeInclusive)</code></a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/155750" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/155750/hovercard">Document that <code>ManuallyDrop</code>'s <code>Box</code> interaction has been fixed</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/156908" data-hovercard-type="issue" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/issues/156908/hovercard">Stabilize LoongArch CRC Intrinsics</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/154645" data-hovercard-type="issue" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/issues/154645/hovercard">The <code>derive</code> macro is available at <code>{core,std}::derive</code>.</a> This was previously <a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/159856" data-hovercard-type="issue" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/issues/159856/hovercard">unintentionally stabilized in 1.96</a>, but is now <a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/154645" data-hovercard-type="issue" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/issues/154645/hovercard">explicitly accepted</a> as a stabilized API.
<ul>
<li>Please note that the MSRV for <code>{core,std}::derive</code> will be 1.96, and not 1.98.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="user-content-1.98.0-Compatibility-Notes"></a></p>
<h2>Compatibility Notes</h2>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/129543" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/129543/hovercard">If fully elided, lifetime bounds of trait object types may now resolve differently or even get rejected in very specific niche scenarios</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/145108" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/145108/hovercard">Error in more cases of ambiguous imports</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/148799" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/148799/hovercard">Switch the destructors implementation for thread locals on Windows to use Fiber Local Storage (FLS)</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/149195" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/149195/hovercard">Convert some cases of the <code>ambiguous_glob_imports</code> lint into a hard error</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/153513" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/153513/hovercard">Where-bounds of the form <code>Type = Type</code> and <code>Type == Type</code> are no longer syntactically allowed</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/155153" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/155153/hovercard">Ensure Send/Sync is not implemented for std::env::Vars{,Os}</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/155193" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/155193/hovercard">Fix that in some attributes, arguments were not properly rejected</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/155299" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/155299/hovercard"><code>repr(transparent)</code> is now more strict about which fields have "trivial" layout and hence can be ignored: <code>repr(C)</code> types, types with private fields, and <code>#[non_exhaustive]</code> types are no longer considered "trivial"</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/155418" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/155418/hovercard">Correctly check whether types have equal size in <code>transmute()</code> when some <code>repr</code> attributes are involved.</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/155527" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/155527/hovercard">More characters are escaped when printing strings and chars</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/155598" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/155598/hovercard">Implement fast path for <code>derive(PartialOrd)</code> when deriving <code>Ord</code></a> This can break crates in practice where a type's PartialOrd and Ord impls were inconsistent with each other.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/155739" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/155739/hovercard">Add temporary scope to <code>assert_eq</code> and <code>assert_ne</code></a></li>
<li>Closed a hole in the pattern matching <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/patterns.html#constant-patterns" rel="nofollow">structural equality</a> check, preventing cases where a match of a constant would be allowed, despite disagreeing with a manually written <code>PartialEq</code> implementation, when a <code>derive(PartialEq)</code> implementation for that type also exists.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/156928" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/156928/hovercard">On Emscripten the WASM exception handling ABI is now unconditionally used</a> The <code>-Zemscripten-wasm-eh=false</code> flag to switch back to JS exceptions has been removed.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/157201" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/157201/hovercard">The UNSAFE_CODE lint is now consistently emitted for all unsafe attributes</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/157509" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/157509/hovercard">Solaris: remove <code>File::lock</code> implementation, it has the wrong semantics (return "unsupported" instead)</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/158020" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/158020/hovercard">Windows-gnu targets now specify baseline tools versions</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/158372" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/158372/hovercard">rustfmt now discovers module files that are defined in <code>cfg_select!</code></a> This may cause more code to be formatted which was previously ignored.</li>
</ul></content>

    <content type="html"><p><a id="user-content-1.97.0-Language"></a></p>
<h2>Language</h2>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/148214" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/148214/hovercard">Consider <code>Result&lt;T, Uninhabited&gt;</code> and <code>ControlFlow&lt;Uninhabited, T&gt;</code> to be equivalent to <code>T</code> for must use lint</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/149509" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/149509/hovercard">Add allow-by-default <code>dead_code_pub_in_binary</code> lint for unused pub items in binary crates</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/154510" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/154510/hovercard">Stabilize the <code>div32</code>, <code>lam-bh</code>, <code>lamcas</code>, <code>ld-seq-sa</code> and <code>scq</code> target features</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/155006" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/155006/hovercard">Stabilize <code>cfg(target_has_atomic_primitive_alignment)</code></a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/155137" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/155137/hovercard">Allow trailing <code>self</code> in imports in more cases</a></li>
</ul>
<p><a id="user-content-1.97.0-Platform-Support"></a></p>
<h2>Platform Support</h2>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/152443" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/152443/hovercard">nvptx64-nvidia-cuda: drop support for old architectures and old ISAs</a></li>
</ul>
<p>Refer to Rust's <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustc/platform-support.html" rel="nofollow">platform support page</a> for more information on Rust's tiered platform support.</p>

<p><a id="user-content-1.97.0-Cargo"></a></p>
<h2>Cargo</h2>

<p><a id="user-content-1.94.0-Cargo"></a></p>
<h2>Cargo</h2>
<ul>
<li>Stabilize the config include key. The top-level include config key allows loading additional config files, enabling better organization, sharing, and management of Cargo configurations across projects and environments. <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/cargo/reference/config.html#including-extra-configuration-files" rel="nofollow">docs</a> <a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/pull/16284" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/cargo/pull/16284/hovercard">#16284</a></li>
<li>Stabilize the pubtime field in registry index. This records when a crate version was published and enables time-based dependency resolution in the future. Note that crates.io will gradually backfill existing packages when a new version is published. Not all crates have pubtime yet. <a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/pull/16369" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/cargo/pull/16369/hovercard">#16369</a> <a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/pull/16372" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/cargo/pull/16372/hovercard">#16372</a></li>
<li>Cargo now parses <a href="https://toml.io/en/v1.1.0" rel="nofollow">TOML v1.1</a> for manifests and configuration files. Note that using these features in Cargo.toml will raise your development MSRV, but the published manifest remains compatible with older parsers. <a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/pull/16415" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/cargo/pull/16415/hovercard">#16415</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/pull/16421/" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/cargo/pull/16421/hovercard">Make <code>CARGO_BIN_EXE_&lt;crate&gt;</code> available at runtime </a></li>
</ul>
<p><a id="user-content-1.94.0-Compatibility-Notes"></a></p>
<h2>Compatibility Notes</h2>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/136776" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/136776/hovercard">Forbid freely casting lifetime bounds of <code>dyn</code>-types</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/138961" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/138961/hovercard">Make closure capturing have consistent and correct behaviour around patterns</a> Some finer details of how precise closure captures get affected by pattern matching have been changed. In some cases, this can cause a non-move closure that was previously capturing an entire variable by move, to now capture only part of that variable by move, and other parts by borrow. This can cause the borrow checker to complain where it previously didn't, or cause <code>Drop</code> to run at a different point in time.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/139493" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/139493/hovercard">Standard library macros are now imported via prelude, not via injected <code>#[macro_use]</code></a> This will raise an error if macros of the same name are glob imported. For example if a crate defines their own <code>matches</code> macro and then glob imports that, it's now ambiguous whether the custom or standard library <code>matches</code> is meant and an explicit import of the name is required to resolve the ambiguity. One exception is <code>core::panic</code> and <code>std::panic</code>, if their import is ambiguous a new warning (<a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/147319" data-hovercard-type="issue" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/issues/147319/hovercard"><code>ambiguous_panic_imports</code></a>) is raised. This may raise a new warning (<a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/147319" data-hovercard-type="issue" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/issues/147319/hovercard"><code>ambiguous_panic_imports</code></a>) on <code>#![no_std]</code> code glob importing the std crate. Both <code>core::panic!</code> and <code>std::panic!</code> are then in scope and which is used is ambiguous.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/146377" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/146377/hovercard">Don't strip shebang in expression-context <code>include!(…)</code>s</a> This can cause previously working includes to no longer compile if they included files which started with a shebang.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/147984" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/147984/hovercard">Ambiguous glob reexports are now also visible cross-crate</a> This unifies behavior between local and cross-crate errors on these exports, which may introduce new ambiguity errors.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/148477" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/148477/hovercard">Don't normalize where-clauses before checking well-formedness</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/148756" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/148756/hovercard">Introduce a future compatibility warning on codegen attributes on body-free trait methods</a> These attributes currently have no effect in this position.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/148825" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/148825/hovercard">On Windows <code>std::time::SystemTime::checked_sub_duration</code> will return <code>None</code> for times before the Windows epoch (1/1/1601)</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/149192" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/149192/hovercard">Lifetime identifiers such as <code>'a</code> are now NFC normalized</a>.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/149709" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/rust-lang/rust/pull/149709/hovercard">Overhaul filename handling for cross-compiler consistency</a> Any paths emitted by compiler now always respect the relative-ness of the paths and <code>--remap-path-prefix</code> given originally. One side-effect of this change is that paths emitted for local crates in Cargo (path dependencies and workspace members) are no longer absolute but relative when emitted as part of a diagnostic in a downstream crate.</li>
</ul>

</ul></content>
